summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests whether cyclophosphamide, bortezomib, and maraviroc can prevent graft-versus-host disease after a half-matched bone marrow transplant in people with HIV and blood cancers. Patients receive preparation drugs for about 2 weeks before the transplant and other drugs after it, and they stay in the hospital for 6 weeks or longer. The first phase checks whether the drug combination is safe, and the second phase checks how well it protects against graft-versus-host disease.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa si la ciclofosfamida, el bortezomib y la maraviroc pueden prevenir la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped después de un trasplante de médula ósea con donante medio compatible, en personas con VIH y cánceres de la sangre. Los pacientes reciben medicamentos de preparación durante unas 2 semanas antes del trasplante y otros medicamentos después, y permanecen en el hospital por 6 semanas o más. La primera fase revisa si la combinación de medicamentos es segura, y la segunda fase revisa qué tan bien protege contra la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped.
who_for: Adults and older teens living with HIV whose viral load is under 400 copies/mL on a stable HIV regimen
Hematologic malignancy with a standard indication for transplant, such as certain leukemias, lymphomas, or myelodysplastic syndrome
Karnofsky performance score of at least 50 percent
At least one potentially suitable half-matched (haploidentical) family or related donor
Adequate heart, lung, liver, and kidney function
not_for: Leukemia or myeloma not in remission, or lymphoma not responding to treatment
Pregnancy, or breastfeeding without willingness to stop before treatment
Known prohibitive allergy to any study drug
Active psychiatric disorder that could affect compliance with the transplant plan
